notes: Water from lakes and rivers: look at the water and press F to drink, or hold an empty bottle and press F to fill it. The prompt says what kind of water it is (not on Hardcore). The sea is salt: you spit it out.

Dirty water can make you ill (a bottle from a lake is about a coin flip). A few hours later your stomach cramps; one bottle passes by itself, more turns into a fever with vomiting, thirst and short breath, and a severe illness can kill. Boil water at a campfire with a pot first to stay safe. Throwing up is loud.

Antibiotic tablets (rare: bathroom cabinets, car boots, hikers' bags, caches, the helicopter wreck and the dam station lab). Take one, wait a few hours, take the next and finish the strip; too soon and it comes back up. They do nothing against the bite.
Water bottles leave an empty bottle when you drink them.
When you die, everything you carried lies in a bag where you fell. Anyone can open it, and it stays for two game days (four on Casual). On Hardcore your things are lost.

Zombies near you now find their way: round hedges, fences and house corners, through gates and garden paths, instead of pushing against them. A chasing pack reaches the house you ran into. Lakes, rivers and the sea are not walkable for them (a bridge is).
Lit rooms draw zombies at night: a lamp left on shows through the windows and nearby zombies come to look. Boarded windows hide the light, and the blackout ends it.
Zombies can no longer bite through walls, closed doors or closed windows.
A zombie bite now makes a sound, for you and for anyone nearby.
Windows in the village houses open and close (F from inside); they swing outward. Boarded-up windows stay shut. Opening one makes a little noise.
A locked front door can now be opened from inside the house: press F to unlock and open it. From outside it stays locked.
Stepping out of a house no longer leaves the street looking dark for seconds: the eye adapts in about a second, and daylight outside is brighter.
A proper television in the living rooms; it stands in the middle of its bench instead of hanging off the end.
Plates, cutlery and food sit on the tables and counters instead of hanging in the air beside them, and no bread is left in the kitchen sink.
A chest of drawers no longer faces the stairwell.
Footsteps inside some houses (the red one on the main road among them) no longer sound like walking on metal.
Every item in the inventory now has a picture instead of only its name.
Double-clicking clothing puts it on. If you already wear something there, the two swap.
A weapon no longer wears down on blows that do nothing: a swing at another player with PvP off, or the wrong tool on a tree or rock.
Your empty right hand no longer floats into view when you jump while holding something.
The world is saved within a couple of seconds when a player leaves, and shortly after a death (before, a leaving player's state stayed in memory until the next autosave).
Playing without Steam: you now keep the same survivor on a friend's server from one launch to the next (before, a second copy of the game on the same PC got a new survivor every time).

The game statistics sent to the dashboard now include the graphics card, processor, memory and the 95th percentile frame time, so slow machines can be told apart from a slow build. Nothing personal is added; the settings switch still turns everything off.
Zombies cannot yet vault hedges or cross rivers by fords; they walk round or wait for a bridge.
The water and illness numbers are first guesses and will be tuned.
